storylines.title: The Fed spent three years cutting. It just reversed course entirely
storylines.observation: The Federal Reserve raised its benchmark rate a quarter point to 3.75%-4% - its first hike since 2023 - after August inflation data came in hotter than expected, sending the 10-year Treasury yield above 5% for the first time since 2007.
storylines.question: What does it cost a central bank to admit, three years into cutting, that inflation was never actually beaten?
storylines.hidden_question: Is this one hike a correction, or the first move in a cycle the Fed will need several more votes to finish?
storylines.pattern: a policy reversal arriving only after the data made the prior stance impossible to maintain
storylines.why_now: Three cycles running of dedicated searches have failed to surface anything dated past Oct 7 that isn't a repeat of already-captured minutes coverage or contaminated with other FOMC cycles (2016, 2017, 2022, last July's meeting). Going dormant at the 3-day edge rather than force a stale bump; reactivating on the next clean, dated Fed development - a Powell speech, new jobs/inflation data, or movement toward the Oct 27-28 meeting.

history.note: The minutes are out: all participants backed the hike, but for different reasons - some targeting demand-driven inflation, others worried about energy and AI-driven price shocks. Most want one more hike before year-end, but stopped short of signaling October specifically; odds now favor a hold.

storylines.title: The takeover was peaceful. The war that followed wasn't
storylines.observation: Tigray forces seized the airports at Mekelle, Axum and Shire from Ethiopia's federal police overnight without a shot fired, prompting Ethiopian Airlines to suspend flights to the region - days after the TPLF and six other armed groups declared an alliance to overthrow the government.
storylines.question: What does a peaceful takeover of a government's own infrastructure say about how much control that government actually had to begin with?
storylines.hidden_question: Is this the opening move of a second Tigray war, or a calculated show of force meant to extract concessions without firing one?
storylines.pattern: an armed faction demonstrating control not through violence but through the quiet capture of the infrastructure a government relies on to reach its own territory
storylines.why_now: Repeated searches this cycle and the last two keep surfacing the same Oct 2-6 window already captured, or contaminated material from the 2020-2022 war and unverifiable claims (an 'Oct 24 AU peace talks' lead and an 'Amhara Fano disrupting supply lines' lead both traced to other years when checked). The war is almost certainly still active - this is a sourcing gap, not a resolution - going dormant rather than bump on unverifiable material; reactivating the moment a clean, freshly-dated development surfaces.
storylines.location: Mekelle, Alamata, Afar and Amhara, Ethiopia

history.note: Taking Mekelle wasn't the end point: federal forces and the Tigray Peace Force pushed north from the captured capital and stepped up airstrikes on other TPLF-held population centers, per a security review covering Oct 2-6 - the campaign widening rather than winding down.

storylines.title: The IMF loan came with one condition. Bolivia's truckers just found out what it costs
storylines.observation: Bolivia raised diesel prices 83% on Sept 19 - from Bs9.80 to Bs17.95 a liter - to satisfy an IMF loan condition ending fuel subsidies. Transport unions answered with a 24-hour nationwide strike Sept 28; bus fares have jumped up to 125%.
storylines.question: Who ends up paying the price when a loan's condition and a country's cost of living collide?
storylines.hidden_question: Is this the start of a manageable adjustment, or the opening act of the kind of unrest that has toppled Bolivian governments before?
storylines.pattern: an externally-imposed economic condition landing first on the population least able to absorb it
storylines.why_now: No report found of what actually happened on Evo Morales's announced Oct 13 protest start, despite searching specifically for it, nor any outcome from Santa Cruz's Oct 10 deadline across three cycles now. Going dormant rather than re-bump the same Oct 11 fact as if it were new; reactivating as soon as either deadline's actual outcome is reported.
storylines.season_or_time_context: diesel subsidy ended Sept 19, nationwide strike Sept 28

history.note: The dispute now risks merging with a second front: Evo Morales has called for his own supporters to begin protests Oct 13, three days after Santa Cruz's deadline - and Santa Cruz's own demands turn out not to include Paz's resignation, just fuel imports, tax cuts and more revenue control for the regions.

storylines.title: A Colorado county is suing oil companies for the climate. The Supreme Court just agreed to listen
storylines.observation: The Supreme Court opened its new term Oct 5 with Suncor Energy v. Boulder County - the first case asking whether a county can sue oil companies under state law for climate damages, or whether federal law preempts claims over harm that crosses every border.
storylines.question: Can a single county's lawsuit meaningfully assign blame for a problem caused by a global industry over a century?
storylines.hidden_question: Is this case actually about climate change, or about whether any state court can touch an industry whose harm is inherently global?
storylines.pattern: a local legal claim testing whether a global harm can be assigned local liability
storylines.why_now: Justice Alito recused himself from the case shortly before argument - a notable last-minute development. The court chose this as the very first case of its new term, a deliberate signal about how seriously it's treating the preemption question before anything else this session.
storylines.season_or_time_context: oral arguments heard Oct 5, 2026, opening day of the court's new term

history.note: Suncor's lawyer gave the argument's starkest framing: if Boulder's claims proceed, some 90,000 U.S. municipalities could effectively set national and international energy policy through local jury verdicts - the scale critics say the case was always really about.

A fuller read of the argument complicates the "sympathetic to oil companies" read: justices reportedly voiced doubts about both sides' broad positions, not just Boulder's - and the 4-4 deadlock risk cuts the other way too, since a tie would leave Colorado's ruling (and Boulder's lawsuit) standing by default.

storylines.title: She said she broke a vial of live bacteria. The governor says that's not what happened
storylines.observation: A 28-year-old researcher at Russia's Irkutsk Anti-Plague Institute died after telling hospital staff she'd broken a vial of live bacteria at work. The regional governor calls it 'pneumonia of unknown origin'; a neighboring governor said on social media she died of plague.
storylines.question: What does it mean when the official explanation and an official's own social-media account of the same death don't match?
storylines.hidden_question: Is the calm official line protecting public health, or protecting the institute from the consequences of what actually happened inside it?
storylines.pattern: an institution's official account diverging from an insider's own report of what happened to them
storylines.why_now: Nearly 200 people have been placed under medical observation and the hospital that treated her is under quarantine, taking no new admissions or discharges - a scale of precaution that sits oddly next to the official line that nothing dangerous occurred.
storylines.season_or_time_context: death occurred early October 2026, reported Oct 5-6

history.note: The case is officially closed: Gov. Kobzev lifted the quarantine Oct 8, saying nearly 5,000 tests found no dangerous microorganisms and all contacts are healthy. He added a new detail - she'd been vaccinated - but the thing the quarantine was actually about, whether she died of plague, is still exactly as unconfirmed as it was on day one.

WHO says Russian authorities told it no plague case has been recorded in Irkutsk, and all 187 monitored contacts remain symptom-free - yet Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan tightened border health checks anyway, treating the official all-clear as a precaution rather than a settled fact.

storylines.title: Nine nights, nine faces of one goddess. Today the pot that holds her gets planted with grain
storylines.observation: Shardiya Navratri begins today with Ghatasthapana: a sacred kalash installed as Durga's vessel, often packed with soil, coins and grain with barley seeds sown beneath it, opening nine nights devoted to nine successive forms of the goddess - the first being Shailaputri.
storylines.question: What does it mean to represent one deity's power as nine distinct, separately-named forms rather than one continuous figure?
storylines.hidden_question: Does splitting the goddess into nine stages make an otherwise overwhelming concept graspable, or does the division itself quietly change what's actually being worshipped?
storylines.pattern: a single extended devotion broken into discrete, individually-named stages rather than treated as one continuous observance
storylines.why_now: The barley seeds sown beneath today's kalash are a living clock, not just a symbol - they'll have visibly sprouted by the ninth night, turning the festival's end into something that can be checked against what actually grew, not just declared.
storylines.location: India and the Hindu diaspora worldwide
storylines.season_or_time_context: Navratri begins Oct 11, 2026, runs nine nights to Dussehra Oct 20

history.note: Day three belongs to Chandraghanta - named for the bell-shaped half-moon on her forehead, riding a tiger (or in some traditions a lion), and associated with courage rather than any of the gentler virtues the earlier forms carry. Milk or kheer is the customary offering.

Day two belongs to Brahmacharini - not a married goddess but an ascetic one, the unmarried Parvati mid-penance, shown barefoot with a prayer rosary and a water pot instead of any of the weapons or finery the later forms carry. The same day is also Chandra Darshana, the first sighting of the new moon.

Day one belongs to Shailaputri, the mountain's daughter - first of Durga's nine forms, associated in several traditions with the Muladhara (root) chakra, the base the other eight days are said to build on.

storylines.title: The government's fix is scheduled for "end of October." Students are striking again today
storylines.observation: Since mid-September, French students have blockaded or closed up to 1,800 high schools and dozens of university sites over teacher shortages, overcrowded classrooms and crumbling buildings. PM Lecornu's Oct 4 letter deferred actual decisions to "fin octobre" - month's end.
storylines.question: What does it mean when a government's answer to an active protest arrives scheduled for after the protest's own momentum is supposed to have passed?
storylines.hidden_question: Is 'end of October' a genuine timeline for complex fixes, or a deadline picked because it's likely to outlast the news cycle the protests created?
storylines.pattern: an official response that defers the substance of an answer past the span of attention the problem is currently getting
storylines.why_now: Organizers and the government can't even agree on how big the movement is: unions put one march's turnout at 450,000, the Interior Ministry at 256,000 - and neither side is backing down on a fresh joint strike with public-sector workers called for today.
storylines.season_or_time_context: protests began mid-September 2026, ongoing, joint strike called for Oct 13

history.note: Lecornu's own letter set the terms: "before the end of October 2026, the first decisions will be presented with their financing and timetable." A government promising a timetable for a timetable, while students blockade schools in the meantime.
